paper_title: LaSQuE Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through   Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning
caption: Classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks in .

annotations.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy percentages of different models or methods. The vertical axis represents accuracy as a percentage, ranging from 40% to 65%, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5%. The horizontal axis contains categories labeled with different methods: "RoBERTa w/o Exp.," "ExEnt," "LaSQuE (mean)," "LaSQuE," "LaSQuE (syn2real)," and "LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)." Each bar is color-coded according to a legend, with bars colored light gray, blue, orange, green, purple, and dark gray, respectively. The heights of the bars correspond to the accuracy values, approximately reaching approximately 46% mark for "RoBERTa w/o Exp.," around 55% for "ExEnt," around 41.5% for "LaSQuE (mean)" and "LaSQuE," approximately 59% for "LaSQuE (syn2real)," and near 62% for "LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)." The bars are sorted by the order presented in the legend and horizontally emphasized by contrasting colors, but otherwise not highlighted or annotated for emphasis. A legend is placed at the right side of the plot with bar colors and corresponding methods.
